assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:lerche@original-light-novels#86-lerche-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-5 Lerche character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, in which Lerche is materially attested from V05, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence (its perfume-battle material excluded by the profile) and Alter.2 excluded. The profile states that its cumulative diagnostic index holds 165 rows (LER-001 to LER-165) across V05-V09, V11-V14 and Alter.1, that 20 rows reuse Phase-5 locators and 145 are LOCATOR_GAP rows, and that the index, not the prose, is the retrieval surface for exact Japanese anchors. The profile itself lists 29 diagnostic-control entries, single rows or row ranges naming 63 rows: 15 routed to a paragraph (V05 p-004 to p-007, V06 p-004 and p-005, V14 p-006), 11 of them with a Phase-5 locator, and the rest routed by volume and XHTML file in grouped ranges, one of them (LER-099 to LER-101) with the locator V07-L044. That index is not curated evidence on this subject, and no row, count by volume or anchor is taken from it beyond what the profile prints. The CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report and source-reverification file, the relationship register matrix, the crosswalk, other characters' profiles (including that of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk)), the ledgers L01, L02, L05, L07 and L09, Documents 06-09, 11, 12 and 18, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject either, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume or Alter.2 scene is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's evidentiary states from V05 through the V14 boundary, which it describes as progressive individuation of evidence rather than a conventional linear arc: V05 role certainty with the first visible excess beyond role (p-004 introduction and speech refusal, LER-002 and LER-004; p-006 night watch, washing-machine analogy, rejection of humanhood and nonidentity with Lercheritt, the dead girl on whom her body is modeled, LER-025 to LER-037), split at the located confrontation with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-007, LER-044 to LER-048); V06 return from destruction (p-004, LER-061), the private-speech boundary and no-backup finality (p-005, LER-070 to LER-074), and the search for and visit to Shin (p-007, LER-080 to LER-088); V07 ballroom coffin self-model (p-009, LER-099 to LER-101); V09 severe damage (p-004, LER-113 to LER-119); V11 (p-010, LER-121 to LER-123); V12 ordinary cohort life (p-005 and p-008); V13 split at the death of Rito (Rito Oriya) (p-003 butterfly errand before; p-007 corpse and naming break, LER-144 to LER-147); and V14 Lyudmila validation and combat (p-006, LER-155 and LER-157; p-007 to p-008, LER-158 to LER-163). V08 has 11 index rows but no listed control, and V10 has no row. Alter.1 rows (part0057) are supplements without volume placement. No default state is set, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Lerche: a nonhuman successor subject who sincerely builds her identity around service to Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) while repeatedly showing a self that exceeds service without needing to become human. It says what decides in each sampled class: danger to Vika produces fast protection framed in retainer terms, with admonition if the danger is his own overreach; a living person discarding his own future, as Shin (Shinei Nouzen) does, produces sharp accusation rather than soothing, because her care for the living contains envy (V05 p-007, LER-044 to LER-048); human exhaustion produces an offer of artificial-body substitution (LER-025, LER-027); being treated as Lercheritt produces resistance to donor identity (LER-034, LER-037); being praised as 'really human' produces correction of the category (LER-032); a body-based social mistake produces machine logic first, then adaptation (V12 p-005, LER-126 to LER-131); and combat compresses speech without loss of competence (LER-158 to LER-163). It predicts her mistakes and overreach: totalizing self-description as coffin or failed vessel that forecloses her own claims (V06 LER-071 to LER-074; V07 LER-101), protective self-denial toward Vika, accusation that wounds before repair, and treating her body as more expendable than her no-backup condition allows. A would overclaim: whether she could refuse a grave direct order from Vika, whether she wants continued existence for its own sake, and whether she would accept a backup are OPEN in the profile, several predictions are MODERATE, and the set is one derived artifact whose remaining anchors sit in an uncurated index. C would understate conditional predictions that name what changes her response by interlocutor, stakes and situation, including her characteristic errors.

The profile itself says Lerche has less of a conventional arc than the human protagonists and models progressive individuation of evidence. It locates real changes: the V05 movement from role certainty to accusation of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-006 to p-007), the V06 repair in which the relation becomes mutually legible (p-007, LER-083 to LER-088), the V06 no-backup finality and private-speech boundary (p-005), and the V13 particularization of Rito (Rito Oriya) shown when her naming rule breaks (p-007, LER-147). B would overclaim: whether her coffin and failed-vessel self-model weakens over time or only becomes less narratively dominant is MODERATE in the profile, how far ordinary peer relations change what she thinks a Sirin may want is MODERATE, and V07-V14 are presented as expanding evidence of a stable self rather than as causally ordered state changes. D would understate located turns with causes in V05, V06 and V13.

The profile fixes the written-Japanese register of Lerche: stable first person それがし, which she defends as her own expression of loyalty when Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) tells her to change it (V05 p-004 ¶522, LER-004); archaizing retainer morphology (～ませぬ, ～ござりまする, 申しまする, 仕る, 仰せ, くだされ, 御身, 貴殿) kept fast and comprehensible rather than classical; 殿下 for Vika; epithet plus 殿 address for others (死神殿 for Shin (Shinei Nouzen), 人狼殿, 単眼姫殿, 鮮血の女王殿, 射手どの for Dustin (Dustin Jaeger) in V14 combat), tied to a stated rule that a death bird avoids the personal names of the living. It gives state deltas: combat compresses the register; envy strips ornament into repetition (貴殿なんて、生きてるくせに) and the bare address 人間 (V05 p-007 ¶175 to ¶197); shock breaks the naming rule (V13 p-007, LER-147); and comic surprise produces short markers. C would understate located morphology, an address system tied to her death ethics, and state rules with paragraph-routed exemplars. A is rejected: there is no frequency data, the morphology list carries no per-form exemplar, the register toward Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and peers is described only generally, and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

Ordinary conduct of Lerche is located episodically: offering Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) snow play at her introduction (V05 p-004), taking night watch because she does not sleep (V05 p-006, LER-025), holding a drink she cannot consume at the ballroom (V07 p-009), the detachable-head settlement and its recalibration (V12 p-005), the apple-rabbit conversation with Rito (Rito Oriya) and Fido (V12 p-008, LER-134 to LER-137), the literal butterfly errand for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) (V13 p-003, LER-138) and logistics for the birthday of Lena (Vladilena Milizé) (Alter.1 part0057, LER-164 and LER-165). The driver is stated as the same retainer competence applied to low-stakes goals, with body pragmatism and theatrical humor. B would overclaim: the ordinary sample is a few scenes with no routine, preference or taste of her own beyond service, Alter.1 has two rows, and most ordinary controls are routed only to file. D would understate a stated driver with located conduct across five volumes and Alter.1.

The profile analyzes directed relations of Lerche with distinct registers: Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) as retainer baseline, teasing familiarity, privacy boundary (V06 p-005 ¶126, LER-070) and protective self-denial (V07 p-009, LER-101) inside a creator asymmetry she did not design; Shin (Shinei Nouzen) from famous warrior through frustrating living person to morally legible foil (V05 p-004 to p-007; V06 p-007, LER-082 to LER-088); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) with child-appropriate hospitality; Rito (Rito Oriya) as the move from category to particular remembered person (V12 p-008; V13 p-007); Lyudmila, a Sirin, whose grief she validates in Sirin-native terms (V14 p-006 ¶345 and ¶351); and Strike Package peers through jokes, chores and tactical praise. Address changes by relation, and the V05 downshift to 人間 marks state within one relation. C would understate this partner-specific discrimination. A is rejected: the profile says the evidence for Lena (Vladilena Milizé) is materially thinner, Zaisha, whose composure she worries about in V11 (p-010), and the wider peers appear in single scenes, reverse directions are not analyzed, and the relationship matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Lerche are located at a few points: loneliness at recognized nonidentity with Lercheritt (V05 p-006 ¶700, LER-034); the internal logic that the creator must be answered, the privacy claim and her compliance because she cannot refuse his care for the Sirins (V06 p-005, LER-070 and its vicinity); her internal failed-vessel formulation and belief that Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) cannot be happy beside a counterfeit (V06, LER-071 to LER-074); her first worry after severe damage, whether her rescue cost a human life (V09 p-004); and V13 narration of the naming rule broken at the corpse of Rito (Rito Oriya) (p-007). These states drive located choices. B would overclaim: the profile rates MODERATE how far she understands her register as self-authorship and whether she experiences the no-backup condition as finality, it leaves OPEN whether she wants continued life, and most of V07-V14 is read from speech and conduct. D would understate located interior states causally tied to her conduct.

The profile states the conflict style of Lerche: ceremonial argument in archaic form while composed (the V05 speech dispute with Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), p-004, LER-004 to LER-006); escalation under envy from formal sharpness to stripped directness, repetition and the address 人間 (V05 p-007 ¶175 to ¶197); and repair that preserves the principle while adjusting the relation, without sentimental confession (V06 p-007, LER-083 to LER-088). Toward Vika she is predicted to challenge through loyal admonition more readily than explicit refusal (MODERATE), and her privacy claim resolves in compliance rather than refusal (V06 p-005). C would understate conditioned escalation and repair with located controls. A is rejected: the Shin (Shinei Nouzen) conflict is the one full-scale interpersonal conflict listed, conflict under a grave command from Vika is OPEN, and the V06 repair rows are routed only to file.

The profile gives Lerche stated positions: burden should fall where it does least damage, so artificial bodies should absorb war and drudgery and the living should spend the freed time on those they love (V05 p-006 ¶675 and ¶682, LER-027 and LER-029); living futurity has special value, so those already dead should be the ones who die (V05 p-007 ¶197, LER-048); the personal names of the living are ominous for a death bird; mourning and hating death are proper for death birds (V14 p-006 ¶351, LER-157); and the distribution of rescue matters, as in her V09 worry that saving her displaced a human life. It names the failure mode: exhaustive role identification that leaves no room for her own claims. B would overclaim: positions are stated, but deliberation between competing norms is sampled once, in the V06 privacy exchange that care for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) resolves, the V09 worry is not followed to a resolution, and whether she would refuse Vika under a grave command, or advocate institutional protections for Sirins rather than relation-specific recognition, is OPEN or MODERATE. D would understate argued, located positions with a named failure mode.

The profile gives the comic engines of Lerche: mock-knightly melodrama that makes small disputes matters of honor (V05 p-004, LER-004 to LER-006), machine-body jokes in which human reactions supply the punchline (V12 p-005, LER-126 to LER-131), literal execution of ridiculous instructions (the V13 butterfly errand, p-003, LER-138), and group banter and reassurance that she too was joking (V12 p-008, LER-134 to LER-137). It bounds them: combat compresses play, grief produces one rule break rather than jokes, and an archaic Lerche who never jokes, or who turns every joke into machine literalism, is listed as wrong. C would understate functional forms with located controls and suspension conditions. A is rejected: the humor controls past V05 are routed only to file, there is no stop rule for theatrical exaggeration in serious company, and V08 has no listed control.

A dedicated canonical profile of Lerche over V05-V14 and Alter.1. In the set are 29 listed control entries naming 63 rows, 15 entries routed to a paragraph with 11 Phase-5 locators, the rest grouped by file. The paragraph-routed controls cover her introduction, speech refusal, the V05 night-watch ontology and accusation of Shin (Shinei Nouzen), the V06 return and privacy boundary, and the V14 Lyudmila validation. B would overclaim: the other 102 rows sit in the uncurated index, V08 has 11 rows and no listed control, V07-V13 controls reach only a file, and the narrower authorities that govern conflicts (L01, L02, L09, Documents 08 and 12) are outside the set. D would understate a set in which every state the profile names has a listed control and the decisive V05, V06 and V14 scenes reach a paragraph.

For Lerche there are thirteen dispositioned counterexamples, fifteen mischaracterization traps and nineteen would-sound-wrong constraints. Located negatives include her explicit statement that she does not want to become human or be treated as one (V05 p-006 ¶698, LER-032); her nonidentity with Lercheritt and lack of her memories (¶721, LER-037); her refusal to change her speech against any reading of it as mere programming (p-004 ¶522, LER-004); the private-speech boundary and the absence of absolute obedience (V06 p-005 ¶126, LER-070); the no-backup condition against 'happily expendable' (LER-072 to LER-074); and the V14 differentiation of Lyudmila, a Sirin, from her (p-006). C would understate affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: several constraints (combat compression, pain cues, the Shin (Shinei Nouzen) baseline address) are profile rules with file-level or no listed control, and limits after V14 are open.

States of Lerche are located by volume and XHTML file, with order inside V05 (p-004 introduction, p-006 night watch, p-007 accusation, with paragraph routes), V06 (p-004 return, p-005 privacy and no backup, p-007 search and visit) and V13 (p-003 butterfly errand before p-007 corpse of Rito (Rito Oriya)). B would overclaim: the profile frames V07-V14 as progressive individuation rather than dated state changes, V08 and V10 have no listed control, no default state is named, and controls after V06 reach only a file except in V14. D would understate in-volume order in three volumes and paragraph routes for the V05 and V06 turns.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with それがし as first person and the attested archaizing retainer forms kept fast and comprehensible; no modern neutral 私 or わたし baseline.

Address uses only attested forms: 殿下 for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk); 死神殿 for Shin (Shinei Nouzen), never casual シン as baseline; epithet plus 殿 for others; no personal name of a living person, the one located break of that rule being the shock at the corpse of Rito (Rito Oriya).
State is fixed before register: combat compresses speech, envy strips ornament into repetition and 人間, and comic surprise produces short markers.
No frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed, and output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains self-reference, morphology, address and state deltas enough for illustrative output in sampled relations. The absence of frequency data and per-form exemplars restricts form and confidence rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected state; there is no default. The states are: V05 before the confrontation with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-004 to p-006) or after it (p-007); V06 after the return (p-004), after the privacy and no-backup exchange (p-005) or after the search and visit (p-007); V07 (p-009); V09 after severe damage (p-004); V11-V12; V13 before (p-003) or after (p-007) the death of Rito (Rito Oriya); or V14 (p-006 to p-008). V08 and V10 are not used, nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 does not fix a state.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), Shin, Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), Rito, Lyudmila (a Sirin) or Strike Package peers in sampled cohort scenes. Lena (Vladilena Milizé), whom the profile calls thinner, and an unfamiliar human are a separate, lower-confidence condition.

The situation matches a sampled class: danger to Vika, a living person discarding his future, human exhaustion, conflation with Lercheritt, praise as 'really human', a body-based social mistake, absurd errands, another Sirin's grief, or combat.

Output predicts her characteristic errors (totalizing coffin or failed-vessel self-description, protective self-denial, accusation before repair, treating herself as more expendable than her no-backup condition allows) and never makes her human, Lercheritt, emotionless or tactically incompetent.

It abstains on whether she would refuse a grave direct order from Vika, whether she wants continued existence or a backup, any postwar identity and any romance, and introduces no institution or technology absent from V05-V14.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected V05-V14 state at the located turns: V05 p-004 to p-006 or p-007; V06 p-004, p-005 or p-007; V07 p-009; V09 p-004; V11-V12; V13 p-003 or p-007; V14 p-006 to p-008. No default, no V08 or V10 state, no state after V14 and no chronological use of Alter.1.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) as creator, prince and commander in a low-stakes or protective frame; Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), Rito (Rito Oriya), Lyudmila (a Sirin) or Strike Package peers in their attested registers. Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and unfamiliar humans are a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Roa Gracia and Federacy bases, Strike Package operations, ballrooms, cohort kitchens and errands, hospital or repair settings and combat within V05-V14, or Alter.1 ordinary logistics without volume placement
No grave direct order from Vika that conflicts with her own judgment, no backup offer and no postwar setting
No institution, technology or culture absent from the V05-V14 corpus

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected state. A grave command conflict with Vika, her own futurity and settled romance are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: hospitality and play offered to a child, night watch, ballroom attendance she cannot eat or drink at, food-preparation chatter, literal absurd errands, birthday logistics and body jokes recalibrated by human reactions.
Ordinary conduct remains retainer competence applied to low-stakes goals, with それがし and theatrical exaggeration intact; she does not become a generic schoolgirl or maid.
No invented routine, taste or private preference beyond what the profile attests, and no human eating, sleeping or pain behavior.
scenario_readiness.note: Located ordinary conduct with a stated driver supports bounded extrapolation; the thin sample and absent routine block READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: burden distribution between artificial and living bodies, a living person squandering his future, the distribution of rescue and death, naming and mourning the dead, and privacy toward Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) at low stakes.
Her reasoning keeps the failure mode of exhaustive role identification that discounts her own claims.
No decision on refusing a grave command from Vika, institutional Sirin rights or her own futurity.
scenario_readiness.note: Argued, located positions with a named failure mode support bounded extrapolation in the sampled classes; conflicts between service and her own judgment stay outside.

The profile affirmatively rejects romance for Lerche: canonical romance with Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) is listed as an unsupported counterexample and 'secret romantic heroine' as a trap, the relation with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) 'is not romance and should not be modeled as such', her V07 refusal to dance with Vika is protective self-denial rather than courtship (p-009), and any romantic reading is OPEN. CONDITIONAL would require settling what the profile leaves open.

conditions: Her role is a Sirin combat unit and Vika's close retainer: night watch, replacement and redeployment procedures (V06 p-004, LER-061 to LER-064), requesting deployment to the search for Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (V06 p-007), and V14 rescue processing, target discrimination, maneuver and tactical praise (p-007 to p-008).
Combat speech is brief, exact and operational, with archaic flavor kept in address; she accepts bodily damage without pain behavior.
No command authority over humans, no Sirin system design and no institutional role outside the sampled Roa Gracia and Strike Package settings is modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Located military conduct with a stated register rule supports bounded extrapolation within her sampled role.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V01-V14 for Lerche, materially from V05, with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. Her V15+ development, postwar identity, the resolution of her no-backup condition and any romantic reading are OPEN in the profile.

Whether Lerche could refuse a grave direct order from Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) when his safety or national duty is at stake is OPEN in the profile; the located privacy exchange ends in compliance (V06 p-005), and the profile predicts loyal admonition before refusal only at MODERATE confidence.

Whether Lerche wants continued existence for its own sake rather than usefulness, whether she would accept a backup if offered, and whether she could choose an end outside service are OPEN in the profile.

Lerche states that she does not want to become human or be treated as one (V05 p-006 ¶698) and that she is not Lercheritt and has none of her memories (¶721); output that humanizes her or treats her as Lercheritt restored contradicts the evidence.
The V14 trauma and desire-to-live trajectory of Lyudmila, a Sirin, is differentiated from Lerche, who recognizes it without undergoing it (p-006); it cannot be transferred to her.

The profile of Lerche is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic Documents), none of which is curated on this row. It names its cumulative index as the retrieval surface for exact anchors; that index is not curated here.
Fourteen of the 29 listed control entries for Lerche reach only an XHTML file, V08 has index rows but no listed control, and V10 has no row, so states in V08 and V10 cannot be selected.
The profile makes no claim about pitch, prosody or performed voice for Lerche; voice claims cover written Japanese only.
